provenance: Digitized rebound curves from Mathavan, Jackson & Parkin 2010, 'A theoretical analysis of billiard ball dynamics under cushion impacts', Proc. IMechE Part C 224(9) 1863-1873, DOI 10.1243/09544062JMES1964. Fig 7 (p.1870/PDF p.8) is CAMERA-MEASURED experimental data (machine-vision, Riley Renaissance snooker table); Figs 8-10 (pp.1870-1871/PDF pp.8-9) are the paper's NUMERICAL curves from its 3D impulse model calibrated to that experiment (ee=0.98, muw=0.14, RMS-fit p.1870). These are the only camera-validated quantitative cushion anchors until first-party footage exists. EQUIPMENT IS SNOOKER (52.5 mm ball, L-profile cushion, h=7R/5): tests MUST construct snooker-parameter scenarios (paper ball M=0.1406 kg, R=0.02625 m; cushion nose height 7R/5=0.03675 m -- the one geometry where 7R/5 is CORRECT, see docs/research/gap-k66-cushion-params.md sec 1) and MUST NOT reuse these numbers for pool (WPA 1.27R). Digitization: PDF fetched 2026-07-02 from https://drdavepoolinfo.com/physics_articles/Mathavan_IMechE_2010.pdf; pages rendered at 600 dpi (pdftoppm), axis frames + tick marks pixel-calibrated (y-tick residuals < 0.01 units), series extracted by color/connected-component pixel clustering with manual disambiguation of legend/annotation overlap; uncertainties are per-series estimates (>= half a minor gridline or marker radius, whichever is larger).

paper.title: A theoretical analysis of billiard ball dynamics under cushion impacts
paper.authors: S. Mathavan, M. R. Jackson, R. M. Parkin
paper.journal: Proc. IMechE Part C: J. Mechanical Engineering Science 224(9), pp. 1863-1873
paper.digitization_method: pdftoppm 600 dpi render + PIL pixel-cluster & per-column color sampling, frame/tick calibrated

equipment.warning: SNOOKER equipment (52.5 mm ball). Assertion tests must build snooker-parameter scenarios; never assert these values against pool (WPA) geometry.
equipment.table: Riley Renaissance-type snooker table (World Snooker Association official brand)
equipment.cushion_nose_height_rule: h = 7R/5 (sin(theta)=2/5), the paper's snooker cushion geometry; correct HERE and only here
equipment.repo_snooker_constants_note: docs/research/pooltool-physics.md table lists snooker m=0.140 kg, R=0.02619 m (pooltool defaults); the paper's own values (0.1406 kg, 0.02625 m) take precedence for these scenarios

model_fit.fit: RMS error minimum over 0..1 x 0..1 grid in 0.01 steps, incident speeds V0 < 1.5 m/s (p.1870)

equipment.angle_convention: incident/rebound angles measured from the cushion line: 0 deg = glancing, 90 deg = perpendicular; rebound angle > 90 deg = ball returns to the side it came from (Fig 11)

figures.conditions: rolling arrival (w0T = V0/R), no sidespin, perpendicular incidence (alpha = 90 deg); machine-vision camera measurement
figures.notes: Overlapping markers merged to cluster centroids. Point ratios run ~0.87-0.95 below 2.5 m/s and ~0.80-0.85 above; the paper's stated 0.818 'average equivalent COR' (p.1867) is its own summary of this experiment. Points above 2.5 m/s exceed the paper's rigid-cushion validity domain.

figures.conditions: rolling arrival (w0T = V0/R), no sidespin; one series per incident speed V0 [m/s]; x = incident angle [deg]
figures.notes: Speed loss is largest near 40-45 deg incidence for every V0 (paper p.1871: 'for any given speed-spin conditions, the speed loss is largest for the ball incident angles around 40 deg').

figures.conditions: rolling arrival (w0T = V0/R), no sidespin; rebound angle is independent of V0 (single curve for all speeds)
figures.notes: Rebound angle grows monotonically and sits above the incident angle for mid-range incidence (ball shortens off the cushion).

figures.conditions: V0 = 1 m/s, no sidespin, topspin w0T = k*V0/R (k=-1 bottom spin, 0 stun, 1 natural roll, 2 overspin); x = incident angle [deg]
figures.notes: Overspin rebounds fastest; with k=2 at 90 deg incidence the rebound speed reaches the incident speed (paper p.1871). Stun (k=0) loses the most speed, min ~0.756 at ~45 deg. k=-1 points below 20 deg overlap the k=1 curve (wider uncertainty).

series.label: k=2 overspin
series.scheme_inconsistency_note: PAPER-FIGURE-vs-PAPER-EQUATIONS inconsistency (cushion-v3 integration, 2026-07-02): at alpha 20-40 deg the published Fig 9a k=2 curve dips to ~0.834, but the paper's own eqs (12)-(14) predict 0.915-0.947 (verified: port matches pooltool solve() to <1e-8; Delta-p converged to 2e-6; eqs 15a/15b friction-nulling has no effect here because nose slip never ceases, min |s|=1.20 m/s). The paper's own text contradicts its figure: p.1871 'when the ball is overspinning ... its rebound tends to be generally higher', yet the printed k=2 curve dips BELOW k=1. Digitization re-verified against a 300 dpi render on 2026-07-02: the curve really prints ~0.834. These 5 points are excluded from the paper anchor and pinned to the scheme's values in scheme_vs_paper_figure_inconsistency_pinned.

figures.conditions: V0 = 1 m/s, no sidespin, topspin w0T = k*V0/R; x = incident angle [deg]
figures.notes: Rebound angles are not greatly affected by topspin (paper p.1871): all four curves lie within a ~9 deg band mid-range, ordered stun >= natural roll >= overspin. k=-1 tracks k=0/k=1 closely and is not separately digitized (crowded panel).

figures.conditions: V0 = 1 m/s, rolling (w0T = V0/R), sidespin w0S = k*V0/R (k>0 right spin, k<0 left spin); x = incident angle [deg]
figures.notes: Right spin (k=2) makes the rebound speed EXCEED the incident speed (max ~1.115 at 40-45 deg); heavy left spin (k=-2) exceeds it near 90 deg. k=-2 coincides with k=0 below ~60 deg (merged markers). k=2 at 90 deg partially occluded by k=-2 (u 0.02).

figures.conditions: V0 = 1 m/s, rolling (w0T = V0/R), sidespin w0S = k*V0/R; x = incident angle [deg]; rebound angle > 90 deg = ball bounces back to the same side (Fig 11)
figures.notes: SIDESPIN REVERSAL: with left spin the rebound angle crosses 90 deg at steep incidence (k=-2 near ~72 deg, k=-1 near ~76 deg) and reaches ~107/~104 deg at 90 deg incidence. Right spin flattens the rebound (k=2 ends ~64 deg). The figure also draws a horizontal reference line at 90 deg.

series.label: k=2
series.scheme_inconsistency_note: PAPER-FIGURE-vs-PAPER-EQUATIONS inconsistency (cushion-v3 integration, 2026-07-02): at alpha 80/90 deg the published Fig 10b k=2 curve reads 58.8/64.1 deg, but the paper's own eqs (12)-(14) predict 64.4/73.1 deg (verified: port matches pooltool solve() to <1e-8; Delta-p converged to 2e-6; eqs 15a/15b nulling has no effect). The same scenario's SPEED panel (Fig 10a k=2) matches the scheme at every digitized point including 80-90 deg, so a physics term missing from the scheme would have to bend the angle while leaving the speed untouched - implausible; a drafting/plotting artifact in the original figure is the consistent explanation. Digitization re-verified against a 300 dpi render on 2026-07-02. These 2 points are excluded from the paper anchor and pinned to the scheme's values in scheme_vs_paper_figure_inconsistency_pinned.

stated_checks.avg_equivalent_cor_note: Paper p.1867: 'the equivalent coefficient of restitution for a rolling ball perpendicularly colliding with the cushion has a value of 0.818, on average'. The digitized Fig 7a point ratios run ~0.87-0.95 below 2.5 m/s and ~0.80-0.85 above, so 0.818 is recorded as the paper's own summary statistic, not re-derived from this digitization.
